item: Each collect-perf tick says what the extraction lock did (held_frac, wait_rate, holder_age_s), and the tick drops four copies to pay for it
key_paths: src/monitoring/collect_perf.py; src/ingest/lock_stats.py; src/scheduler/process_budget.py; src/monitoring/forensics.py; tests/test_lock_tick_block.py; tests/test_session_forensics.py; tests/process_budget_panel_node_test.js
summary: Every collect-perf tick carries extraction_lock = held_frac, wait_rate and holder_age_s, the differences of two readings of the live gauge (lock_stats.live_reading, merged in PR #1453) over the gauge's own monotonic clock; the baseline is taken when the monitor starts, so the first tick has a delta. The words (lock_stats.LIVE_METHOD, deliberately NOT written to the log): held_frac = share of the tick's wall time some thread held the extraction lock (outermost holds only, 0 to 1); wait_rate = thread-seconds spent waiting for it per wall second (a mean queue length, can exceed 1); holder_age_s = seconds the current holder had held it at the tick's instant, absent when nobody held it (0.0 means a hold just began); both rates are differences of two readings, open holds and open waits included, over the interval between this row's ts and the previous row's (the first tick's is about one interval, from the baseline taken at monitor start); extractions only, the lock and not the CPU, and not which page. Shapes: {held_frac:0.42, wait_rate:1.73, holder_age_s:8.4}; held_frac and wait_rate null with a reason ('no earlier reading', 'no time between readings') and never 0, because 0 would read as 'the lock was idle'; holder_age_s is written on every path that has a reading, the null ones included; an unreadable gauge is {unavailable: <ExceptionClass>} (class only, never the text; a planted secret is pinned out) and the next tick says it has nothing to compare. Differences are not clamped: the totals only grow and the lock is exclusive, so a value outside 0..1 would be evidence an assumption broke. Why it exists: the pass summary is written when the pass ends, so a killed pass (the lxml abort, an out-of-memory kill) or a hang (the 85 s hold of the OPEN_QUEUE) left ticks and no summary, and a hold still open was in no counter while every other extraction waited. PAID FOR IN THE SAME ROWS: the tick drops elapsed_s, process_budget.collector_kbps (equal to the tick's download_rate_kbps on the measured path, pinned against the real producers) and process_budget.mode (equal to rate_mode); process_budget.METHOD goes from 185 to 131 characters and the maximum-mode budget_reason now says the governor steers by measured gain and contention (the old text said only that the governor 'backs off on contention rather than on a rate', which left out that it steers by the articles stored per window, R180). compose and the governor still see the whole dict. forensics.py read the tick's elapsed_s (found by the independent read, not by my grep), so last_collector_sample now carries since_pass_start_s = the tick's ts minus pass_id, null when either cannot be read, never 0; it is time into the pass (the runner stamps pass_id before source selection), not time since the monitor started. BYTES, measured on a log written by the app's own CollectionMonitor._tick and BandwidthGovernor, with the real gauge marks called from one helper thread per simulated collector (the extractions' timing is a queueing-model simulation; the gauge's arithmetic is real), five logs of up to 5,000 rows, before = main 18de125e4, after = this change, through the real debug_bundle: RAW serialised bytes are net negative in all ten diagnostics copies (slim, 17 ticks: -1,088 to -1,283 B; whole, 191 ticks: -11,293 to -15,185 B; the target-mode log keeps 20 and 200 ticks); a tick is 55 to 80 B smaller on average (maximum mode 1,640 to 1,560 B), the block is 52 to 73 B, and the widest block the code can write (79 B) is smaller than the least the four trims save in any tick (107 B), pinned. DEFLATED (the archive compresses), eight of ten copies are net zero or smaller (-1 to -107 B; the same log built twice moves about 30 B): NET-ZERO NOT MET ON THE LOCK-SATURATED PASS, +34 B in the slim copy and +223 B in the whole copy (about 0.9 percent of the copy), because that pass has the highest-entropy block (a standing queue moves wait_rate and holder_age_s on almost every tick, and 86 percent of its ticks carry a holder age), which DEFLATE prices at a few bytes a tick, while the fields dropped were repeats it priced at almost nothing. The first design wrote the defining sentence once on the pass summary and measured +210 to +264 B per slim copy once deflated (a copy taken after a pass holds the summary and the sentence is unique text), so the sentence stays in the code, the tests and this row. #1477's window pin is against a RECORDED least tick (1,552 B), so no edit was needed there; the live least maximum-mode tick in these logs is now 1,534 to 1,542 B and the copies are still smaller than without the block. Cost of a reading: 2.0 microseconds with 14 waiters and 0.97 idle (it takes the gauge's leaf lock, which holding() and released() also take inside every hold), once per tick. NOT VERIFIED: no real maximum-mode diagnostics zip with the gauge exists yet, so the widths and how often a holder age shows are modelled; reading them off the first real zip is 0.5.1 open item (the real-install step). Proof: tests/test_lock_tick_block.py, 33 tests (arithmetic, null paths keep the holder age, a holder age of 0.0 is present, wiring against the real gauge with a fake clock, failure texts carry the class only, the words stay out of the log, the trims, the byte pin), 21 mutants killed; one independent Opus read (it found the forensics reader and the holder age dropped on the null paths, both folded with a red-without test).
